content: 1. Chowdhary N, Rahman A, and Verdeli H discussed strategies to improve access to psychological treatments, drawing lessons from developing countries. Their findings were published in Behaviour Research and Therapy in 2011, volume 49, issue 9, pages 523–528. 2. The World Health Organization (WHO) has developed clinical and policy guidelines to address intimate partner violence and sexual violence against women. These guidelines are accessible through the WHO reproductive health publications. 3. Murray LK, Dorsey S, Skavenski S, Kasoma M, Imasiku M, Bolton P, and colleagues explored the identification, adaptation, and implementation of an evidence-based psychotherapy for children in a low-income country. Their study focused on the use of Trauma-Focused Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (TF-CBT) in Zambia and was published in the International Journal of Mental Health Systems in 2013, volume 7, article 24. 4. Patel V examined the future of psychiatry in lowand middle-income countries, emphasizing the challenges and opportunities in these settings. This work appeared in Psychological Medicine in 2009, volume 39, issue 11, pages 1759–1762. 5. Patel V, Maj M, Flisher AJ, De Silva MJ, Koschorke M, and Prince M conducted a survey for the World Psychiatric Association (WPA) on reducing the treatment gap for mental disorders. Their findings were published in World Psychiatry in 2010, volume 9, issue 3, pages 169–176. 6. San Diego RJ analyzed the process of healing trauma's invisible wounds through a qualitative approach. This study was published in the Asia Pacific Journal of Counselling and Psychotherapy in 2011, volume 2, issue 2, pages 151–170. 7. Saxena S, Thornicroft G, Knapp M, and Whiteford H highlighted the scarcity, inequity, and inefficiency of mental health resources globally. Their analysis was published in The Lancet in 2007, volume 370, issue 9590, pages 878–889. 8. Stoltenborgh M, van IJzendoorn MH, Euser EM, and Bakermans-Kranenburg MJ conducted a meta-analysis to provide a global perspective on the prevalence of child sexual abuse. Their findings were published in Child Maltreatment in 2011, volume 16, issue 2, pages 79–101. 9. Sumner S, Mercy J, Saul J, Motsa-Nzuza N, Kwesigabo G, Buluma R, and colleagues examined the prevalence of sexual violence against children and the utilization of social services across seven countries between 2007 and 2013. Their study was published in the MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report in 2015, volume 64, pages 565–569. 10. Back S and Lips HM investigated factors such as victim age, victim gender, and observer gender in attributing responsibility in cases of child sexual abuse. Their study was published in Child Abuse & Neglect in 1998, volume 22, issue 12, pages 1239–1252. 11. Barker-Collo S and Read J reviewed models of response to childhood sexual abuse and their implications for treatment. Their work was published in Trauma, Violence, & Abuse in 2003, volume 4, issue 2, pages 95–111.
